theorem_title: Remark 3: a small remainder map preserves $a+b=c+d$
natural_language_statement:
If every $a$ in $A$ is written $a = k(a)q + r(a)$ with the remainder small, $4|r(a)| < q$, then $a \mapsto r(a)$ preserves the relation $a + b = c + d$.

The two remainder sums each have absolute value below $q/2$, so their difference has absolute value below $q$; it is also a multiple of $q$, so it is zero.

The constant 4 is the paper's $\alpha$ for the Sidon relation, whose coefficient vector is $(1, 1, -1, -1)$, and every later step of the 1975 route reduces to an application of this remark at some modulus.
source: Janos Komlos, Miklos Sulyok, and Endre Szemeredi, "Linear problems in combinatorial number theory", Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 26 (1975) 113-121, Remark 3
